juce::SoundPlayer Class Reference

## Detailed Description

A simple sound player that you can add to the [AudioDeviceManager](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioDeviceManager.html "Manages the state of some audio and midi i/o devices.") to play simple sounds.

See also[AudioProcessor](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioProcessor.html "Base class for audio processing classes or plugins."), [AudioProcessorGraph](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioProcessorGraph.html "A type of AudioProcessor which plays back a graph of other AudioProcessors.")

* * *

## [◆](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1SoundPlayer.html\#a86a8f75dd4099dc539ec1b3534943efb)play() \[4/5\]

|     |     |     |     |

| void juce::SoundPlayer::play | ( | [PositionableAudioSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1PositionableAudioSource.html) \* | _audioSource_, |
|  |  | bool | _deleteWhenFinished_ = false, |
|  |  | double | _sampleRateOfSource_ = 0.0 ) |

Plays the sound from a positionable audio source.

This will output the sound coming from a positionable audio source. This gives you slightly more control over the sound playback compared to the other playSound methods. For example, if you would like to stop the sound prematurely you can call this method with a [AudioTransportSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioTransportSource.html "An AudioSource that takes a PositionableAudioSource and allows it to be played, stopped,...") and then call audioSource->stop. Note that, you must call audioSource->start to start the playback, if your audioSource is a [AudioTransportSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioTransportSource.html "An AudioSource that takes a PositionableAudioSource and allows it to be played, stopped,...").

The audio device manager will not hold any references to this audio source once the audio source has stopped playing for any reason, for example when the sound has finished playing or when you have called audioSource->stop. Therefore, calling audioSource->start() on a finished audioSource will not restart the sound again. If this is desired simply call playSound with the same audioSource again.

Parameters

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| audioSource | the audio source to play |
| deleteWhenFinished | If this is true then the audio source will be deleted once the device manager has finished playing. |
| sampleRateOfSource | The sample rate of the source. If this is zero, JUCE will assume that the sample rate is the same as the audio output device. |

|  |  | bool | _deleteWhenFinished_ = false, |
|  |  | bool | _playOnAllOutputChannels_ = false ) |

Plays the sound from an audio sample buffer.

This will output the sound contained in an audio sample buffer. If deleteWhenFinished is true then the audio sample buffer will be automatically deleted once the sound has finished playing.

If playOnAllOutputChannels is true, then if there are more output channels than buffer channels, then the ones that are available will be re-used on multiple outputs so that something is sent to all output channels. If it is false, then the buffer will just be played on the first output channels.

| void juce::SoundPlayer::audioDeviceIOCallbackWithContext | ( | const float \*const \* | _inputChannelData_, |
|  |  | int | _numInputChannels_, |
|  |  | float \*const \* | _outputChannelData_, |
|  |  | int | _numOutputChannels_, |
|  |  | int | _numSamples_, |
|  |  | const [AudioIODeviceCallbackContext](https://docs.juce.com/master/structjuce_1_1AudioIODeviceCallbackContext.html) & | _context_ ) | | overridevirtual |

Processes a block of incoming and outgoing audio data.

The subclass's implementation should use the incoming audio for whatever purposes it needs to, and must fill all the output channels with the next block of output data before returning.

The channel data is arranged with the same array indices as the channel name array returned by [AudioIODevice::getOutputChannelNames()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODevice.html#a30bc03f3819dfe0dd8edd96728400111 "Returns the names of all the available output channels on this device."), but those channels that aren't specified in [AudioIODevice::open()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODevice.html#ae2a8aae2ca2eaee6af3dd10a245ffc64 "Tries to open the device ready to play.") will have a null pointer for their associated channel, so remember to check for this.

Parameters

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| inputChannelData | a set of arrays containing the audio data for each incoming channel - this data is valid until the function returns. There will be one channel of data for each input channel that was enabled when the audio device was opened (see [AudioIODevice::open()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODevice.html#ae2a8aae2ca2eaee6af3dd10a245ffc64 "Tries to open the device ready to play.")) |
| numInputChannels | the number of pointers to channel data in the inputChannelData array. |
| outputChannelData | a set of arrays which need to be filled with the data that should be sent to each outgoing channel of the device. There will be one channel of data for each output channel that was enabled when the audio device was opened (see [AudioIODevice::open()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODevice.html#ae2a8aae2ca2eaee6af3dd10a245ffc64 "Tries to open the device ready to play.")) The initial contents of the array is undefined, so the callback function must fill all the channels with zeros if its output is silence. Failing to do this could cause quite an unpleasant noise! |
| numOutputChannels | the number of pointers to channel data in the outputChannelData array. |
| numSamples | the number of samples in each channel of the input and output arrays. The number of samples will depend on the audio device's buffer size and will usually remain constant, although this isn't guaranteed. For example, on Android, on devices which support it, Android will chop up your audio processing into several smaller callbacks to ensure higher audio performance. So make sure your code can cope with reasonable changes in the buffer size from one callback to the next. |
| context | Additional information that may be passed to the [AudioIODeviceCallback](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODeviceCallback.html "One of these is passed to an AudioIODevice object to stream the audio data in and out."). |

Reimplemented from [juce::AudioIODeviceCallback](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODeviceCallback.html#a9ed4465e529f119669e48e9252c4d315).

Called to indicate that the device is about to start calling back.

This will be called just before the audio callbacks begin, either when this callback has just been added to an audio device, or after the device has been restarted because of a sample-rate or block-size change.

You can use this opportunity to find out the sample rate and block size that the device is going to use by calling the [AudioIODevice::getCurrentSampleRate()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODevice.html#a006a610e33f6805f8b33331bc104aef5 "Returns the sample rate that the device is currently using.") and [AudioIODevice::getCurrentBufferSizeSamples()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioIODevice.html#a9f9c0afaff542970832dd1a2ae66c95e "Returns the buffer size that the device is currently using.") on the supplied pointer.

Parameters

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| device | the audio IO device that will be used to drive the callback. Note that if you're going to store this this pointer, it is only valid until the next time that audioDeviceStopped is called. |

inputChannelDataa set of arrays containing the audio data for each incoming channel - this data is valid until the function returns. There will be one channel of data for each input channel that was enabled when the audio device was opened (see AudioIODevice::open())
numInputChannelsthe number of pointers to channel data in the inputChannelData array.
outputChannelDataa set of arrays which need to be filled with the data that should be sent to each outgoing channel of the device. There will be one channel of data for each output channel that was enabled when the audio device was opened (see AudioIODevice::open()) The initial contents of the array is undefined, so the callback function must fill all the channels with zeros if its output is silence. Failing to do this could cause quite an unpleasant noise!
numOutputChannelsthe number of pointers to channel data in the outputChannelData array.
numSamplesthe number of samples in each channel of the input and output arrays. The number of samples will depend on the audio device's buffer size and will usually remain constant, although this isn't guaranteed. For example, on Android, on devices which support it, Android will chop up your audio processing into several smaller callbacks to ensure higher audio performance. So make sure your code can cope with reasonable changes in the buffer size from one callback to the next.
contextAdditional information that may be passed to the AudioIODeviceCallback.

Reimplemented from juce::AudioIODeviceCallback.

overridevirtual

Called to indicate that the device is about to start calling back.

This will be called just before the audio callbacks begin, either when this callback has just been added to an audio device, or after the device has been restarted because of a sample-rate or block-size change.

You can use this opportunity to find out the sample rate and block size that the device is going to use by calling the AudioIODevice::getCurrentSampleRate() and AudioIODevice::getCurrentBufferSizeSamples() on the supplied pointer.

Parameters
devicethe audio IO device that will be used to drive the callback. Note that if you're going to store this this pointer, it is only valid until the next time that audioDeviceStopped is called.
